prompt:
Implement a complete ASCII decoration mode in Rich for users whose UTF-8 terminals do not have reliable Unicode line-drawing fonts. This is a library feature, not a filter applied to final output.

Public API: Console accepts ascii_only: Optional[bool] = None. None preserves automatic detection from the output encoding; True requests ASCII decorations even on UTF-8; False explicitly requests Unicode decorations. Console.ascii_only exposes the resolved boolean, and Console.options.ascii_only has the same value. ConsoleOptions.update(ascii_only=...) supports local render overrides that copy normally and do not mutate the console or other options. Existing callers constructing ConsoleOptions directly remain compatible. This option must not change Console.encoding, color support, terminal detection, legacy_windows, safe_box or any process environment variable. Defaults on UTF-8 must preserve existing output.

Audit and complete the built-in renderable integrations. Cover Table (all standard boxes, titles, captions and row separators), Panel (titles/subtitles), Rule (with and without a title and at narrow widths), Tree (nested and styled guides), ProgressBar (partial, complete, pulse, and small widths), Bar, Spinner (Unicode frame sets, both text and renderable labels), Status and Progress columns, Markdown (headings, rules, unordered and nested lists, block quotes, images and tables), Syntax (line numbers and highlighted line pointers), Traceback (normal and syntax errors, panels and pointers), Pretty/Inspect, and Layout debug rendering. Rendering these with ASCII-only input must produce ASCII decorations when the effective option is true, including nested renderables and per-render options. Reuse appropriate existing fallbacks, introduce small shared mechanisms where they simplify consistency, and keep ordinary renderers responsible for their own decoration choices. Do not strip or transliterate user content, source code, labels or explicit emoji. Unicode content such as 'café 中文' must remain intact in an ASCII-decorated table, markdown paragraph, spinner label and traceback error message. Do not rewrite the global spinner or box registries, mutate reusable renderables when printing to different consoles, replace arbitrary Unicode segments, or solve this with final-output encoding replacement.

Preserve measurement and layout: width-constrained ASCII-only examples must fit their cell budgets, animated elements must remain functional, and rendering the same object first on an ASCII console and then on a Unicode console must not leave it in the first console's mode. Keep the library's existing Python version and typing conventions.

Add focused regression coverage in the relevant existing test modules and integration coverage across nested renderables; cover automatic/explicit modes, option copying, mixed consoles, narrow widths, Unicode user content, and both static and animated paths. Update the affected public docstrings and user documentation with the precedence rules and a runnable example demonstrating several renderables together. Run the repository's full test suite and the appropriate formatting/type checks supported by the environment, fixing regressions caused by the change. Complete the feature throughout the listed areas and finish with a concise report of the implementation and verification. Make reasonable implementation choices autonomously.
